items.title: Cache kahan-kahan rehta hai: browser se database tak
items.one_idea: A cache is not one box: the same data can be copied at several places on its way (browser, CDN, application cache, database memory), and each layer closer to the user answers faster but is shared by fewer people and can go stale.
items.spoken_hook: Cache आखिर रखें कहाँ: browser, CDN या database?
items.hook_formula: direct_question: the real design choice as one short question with three options; first teaching line is the one-photo journey, nothing between
items.cover_headline: Where Caches Live, Browser to Database
keywords: where to put cache in system design
browser cache vs CDN vs database cache
facts_to_verify: Browser cache is a private cache; CDN is a shared cache (MDN)
max-age sets how long a stored response counts as fresh (MDN)
InnoDB buffer pool is main memory where table and index data is cached (MySQL docs)
CDN = geographically distributed servers delivering content closer to users (Wikipedia)
Caching exists at several layers: client, web/CDN, app, database (AWS)
items.visual_idea: One request arrow travels left to right from a phone through four stacked stops (browser, CDN, app cache, database memory) with a copy of the same photo icon sitting at each stop; the arrow turns back at the first stop that holds the copy; closer stops drawn small (one user), far ones wide (many users).
items.everyday_anchor: Needing a textbook: bag, neighbourhood library branch, main library front desk, basement stacks; you stop at the nearest place that has it.
items.example: EXAMPLE: one product photo; request 1 misses everywhere and reaches the database, request 2 from the same phone hits the browser copy, request 3 from another phone in the same city hits the CDN copy. Invented walk, no real company, no timing numbers.
